## Natural history notes

A native perennial herb or small subshrub in the rockrose family, characterized by narrow gray-green leaves and bright yellow, five-petaled flowers. Florida Scrub Frostweed occurs primarily in dry, sandy, fire-maintained habitats such as scrub and xeric sandhill, where it is adapted to intense sunlight and nutrient-poor soils. Although once considered endemic to Florida, it is now known from scattered populations elsewhere in the southeastern coastal plain. The species can produce both showy, insect-pollinated flowers and inconspicuous self-pollinating flowers, providing two pathways for seed production.
